title: Portal billing mirror
description: What Paddle says about a workspace's subscription, and the one change a customer makes to it (portal plan P4.3; spec §Customer experience, D2192). The portal mirrors and never decides: invoices, payment methods and cancellation live in Paddle's own customer portal, and what is here is the state the screens read. Seats are Paddle's quantity on purpose — a seat change updates that one subscription rather than making another, because one workspace has one (D2192). Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_billing.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

subscription.description: One workspace's subscription as the portal last heard it from Paddle.

id.description: Paddle's subscription id, kept as Paddle spells it: it is what a support conversation, a refund and a proration are looked up by, and the mirror exists so that a lookup does not have to reach Paddle.

organisation_id.description: The organisation that pays. Deleting it cancels this subscription and revokes the entitlements' keys (D2195, P2.4).

workspace_id.description: The portal workspace the subscription is for.

state.description: Paddle's own state, spelled as Paddle spells it: the portal's screens and Paddle's customer portal must not describe one subscription two ways.

seats.description: The subscription's quantity, which is what a seat purchase updates (P4.3). The keys follow: the event that carries the new quantity reissues them with the same renewal secret (D2200, P3.6).

price_id.description: Paddle's price this subscription was bought at. It is kept because a price is what a row's tier and term were sold as (P0.2), and a report reads the sale rather than the current catalogue.

starts_at.description: When the subscription began, in UTC, which is the payment's instant the entitlement's term runs from too (D2197).

renews_at.description: When Paddle will next charge, in UTC, or null for a subscription that will not renew. It is Paddle's answer and not the portal's arithmetic: a date this service worked out would be wrong on the first edge case.

ends_at.description: When the paid term ends, in UTC, or null while nothing has ended it. A subscription cancelled part-way through a term carries this and not a state of its own: the customer keeps what they paid for.

cancelled_at.description: When cancellation was recorded, in UTC, or null while none was. It is kept beside ends_at because a cancellation and the end of a term are different instants.

seats.description: An owner's or admin's request to buy more seats (P4.3).
The whole quantity and not an increment: a customer asking for the number they believe they are buying is what makes a request whose reply was lost safe to send again.
